entries.title: The Run
body: Explore rooms, survive fights, claim rewards, and push deeper toward the next boss.
Held embers travel with the run until banked, spent, recovered, or lost.

entries.title: Map and Rooms
body: Revealed exits show where you can travel next. Cleared rooms stay available as routes.
Combat, campfire, merchant, treasure, relic, and boss rooms each change the next choice.

entries.title: Character and Loadout
body: Equipment, attuned magic, item slots, relics, and learned skills shape your deck and tactics.
Most loadout changes happen outside combat, including pre-battle and campfire moments.

entries.title: Rewards
body: After combat, choose a card, take healing, or claim other room rewards when offered.
New magic cards enter reserve first; attune them from the character sheet to add them to the active deck.

entries.title: Relics
body: Relics are passive run modifiers. Some trigger in combat, some change card values, and some alter rewards.
Hover relic badges in the top HUD for their current text.

entries.title: Combat Board
body: Cards resolve against board coordinates. A target is legal only when the card's targeting rule, range, line of sight, occupancy, and terrain checks all pass.
Card previews show legal targets, affected tiles, and projected result values before resolution.

entries.title: Turn Clock
body: Each played card adds its printed time to the acting unit's turn delay.
The turn clock orders actors by current delay and previews the next turns.

entries.title: Card Plays
body: Each player turn begins with a finite card play capacity. Playing a card spends one play unless an effect states otherwise.
Card play effects add temporary capacity that expires at the end of the current player turn.

entries.title: Health and Defenses
body: Non-piercing damage is applied to Block first, then Stoneskin, then health.
Block clears before that actor’s turn-start Fire damage. Stoneskin persists and can absorb it.
Chilled and Frozen modify direct attack damage. Fire terrain damage does not gain these bonuses or trigger direct-hit riders.

entries.title: Defiance
body: Every fourth permanent level grants one Defiance for each new run.
Lethal health loss spends one Defiance to restore 25% max health and continue the same combat.
Defiance never refills during a run. A level milestone reached mid-run adds only the newly earned charge.

entries.title: Targeting
body: Melee actions target adjacent or pattern-defined nearby tiles. Ranged actions require a legal range and line-of-sight path.
Area actions resolve over a tile pattern. Push and pull resolve forced movement along a legal direction until distance, blockers, or terrain stop the target.

entries.title: Fatigue
body: When a draw request empties the draw pile, the discard pile reshuffles into a new draw pile.
Each reshuffle increments fatigue. Fatigue deals direct health loss that bypasses block.

entries.title: Traps
body: Entering or striking a trap triggers its printed damage only on the trap tile. The center hit resolves once per actor, including large actors.

The four cardinal neighbors receive the trap’s elemental surface. An Air trap instead pushes adjacent actors outward. Creating Fire or Ice beneath a stationary actor does not deal damage or apply Chilled.
The preview shows center danger separately from the surrounding terrain wake. All actors share these hazards.

entries.title: Lightning Strikes
body: Lightning strikes resolve direct Lightning hits at previewed tiles.
A Lightning attack can conduct through cardinally connected Electrified terrain, hitting enemy occupants once and consuming the connected region. Gaps require an explicit Chain route.

entries.title: Summons
body: Summon actions create additional enemy units of the configured minion type.
Summoned units enter the normal turn clock, occupy board tiles, and use their own intent definitions.

entries.title: The Umbra
body: The Umbra hides board tiles beyond your current vision. Enemies concealed within it cannot be directly targeted, and their identities, intents, and threat previews remain hidden.
Umbra stages grow more severe deeper in the labyrinth. Radiance effects create light, extend your vision, reveal hidden enemies, or reduce the room's Umbra stage.

entries.title: Melee
body: Melee actions use short-range target rules, usually adjacent to the acting unit.

entries.title: Ranged
body: Ranged actions target distant tiles that pass the action's range and line-of-sight checks.

entries.title: Area Attack
body: Area actions resolve over every legal target tile in their configured pattern.
Some area patterns can rotate around the origin before the action is committed.

entries.title: Move
body: Move walks through reachable passable tiles. Each Rubble tile costs 2 movement to enter; ordinary floor costs 1.
Entering Fire or Ice triggers its surface effect. Previewed paths include movement cost and hazard events. A fresh positive movement allowance always permits one legal first step.

entries.title: Blink
body: Blink relocates directly to a legal destination without crossing intervening tiles.
Only the landing tile triggers surface and trap entry effects. Rubble does not increase Blink range cost.

entries.title: Block
body: Block absorbs non-piercing damage before stoneskin and health.
Block is cleared when that unit begins its next turn.

entries.title: Stoneskin
body: Stoneskin absorbs non-piercing damage after block and before health.
Stoneskin persists across turns until damage or sunder removes it.

entries.title: Heal
body: Heal increases health up to maximum health.
Card persistence after a heal is determined by the card's exhaust or consume fields.

entries.title: Draw
body: Draw moves cards from draw pile to hand up to the requested amount and hand-size limit.

entries.title: Card Play
body: Card play effects increase current-turn card play capacity by the printed amount.

entries.title: Flurry
body: Flurry snapshots every card play available when the card begins.
It repeats the card's printed actions and health cost once per play spent, but pays the card's Time only once. Card plays gained during resolution remain available afterward.

entries.title: Illusion
body: Illusion creates an allied decoy with its printed health. Enemies may target it.
A decoy’s arrival counts as entry for surfaces and traps. Illusions share terrain danger with other actors.

entries.title: Immobilize
body: Immobilize prevents move and blink actions on the affected unit's next turn.
The immobilize flag clears after that turn is processed.

entries.title: Exhaust
body: Exhaust moves the played card to the burned pile instead of discard.
Burned cards do not return to draw or discard for the rest of the combat.

entries.title: Health Cost
body: Health cost is paid when the card is committed.
Health-cost loss bypasses block and stoneskin.

entries.title: Pierce
body: Pierce damage bypasses block and stoneskin.
Bypassed defenses are not reduced by the pierced damage.

entries.title: Bleed
body: Bleed stores a damage value on the affected unit.
Before that unit resolves a real move or attack action, bleed deals its stored damage. The bleed value clears after that unit's next turn.

entries.title: Freeze
body: An Ice attack against an actively Chilled actor applies Freeze after that hit. It consumes all Ice beneath the actor and clears Chilled.
Freeze skips the actor’s next turn and doubles direct attack damage received while Frozen. This replaces the Chilled damage bonus. Passive terrain damage is not doubled.
A Frozen actor cannot refresh Freeze or regain Chilled during its skipped turn. It thaws afterward. Later entry onto Ice or a later normal turn start can activate Chilled again.

entries.title: Shock
body: Shock disrupts the affected unit's next non-movement action.
The shock value decrements during that unit's turn setup.

entries.title: Expose
body: Expose adds its stored value to the next damage hit against the affected unit.
Expose clears after being consumed by a hit.

entries.title: Sunder
body: Sunder removes block first, then stoneskin, up to the printed sunder value.
Sunder resolves before the damage portion of the action.

entries.title: Chain
body: Chain N can jump up to N tiles from each struck enemy or Electrified relay. N is the reach of each jump. Each enemy is struck at most once.
Electrified tiles can bridge a route even when empty. Used relay tiles are consumed. The preview shows the chosen route before the attack resolves.
A damaging Lightning hit can also conduct through one connected Electrified region, reaching its enemy occupants without requiring Chain. Only Chain can cross a gap between conductors.

entries.title: Push
body: Push moves the target away from the action source up to the printed distance.
Forced movement ignores Rubble’s movement surcharge but triggers Fire, Ice and traps on each tile entered. Blockers and occupied tiles can stop it.

entries.title: Pull
body: Pull moves the target toward the action source up to the printed distance.
Forced movement ignores Rubble’s movement surcharge but triggers Fire, Ice and traps on each tile entered. Blockers and occupied tiles can stop it.

entries.title: Consume
body: Consume removes the played item card from the run after resolution.

entries.title: Radiance
body: Radiance cards carry light into the Umbra. Their effects include Illuminate, Vision, Truesight, and Dispel Umbra.
Radiance cards still follow their printed element, targeting, time, and card-play rules.

entries.title: Illuminate
body: Illuminate places a light source on the targeted tile and reveals Umbra within its printed radius.
Its counter shows how many player turns remain. A lasting light displays an infinity symbol instead.

entries.title: Vision
body: Vision temporarily increases the radius of light centered on the player by the printed amount.
The bonus counts down on player turns; when it ends, the Umbra gradually closes over newly hidden tiles.

entries.title: Truesight
body: Truesight reveals enemies through the Umbra and permits direct attacks against them even while their tiles remain dark.
Its player-HUD counter shows how many player turns remain. Truesight does not illuminate board tiles.

entries.title: Dispel Umbra
body: Dispel Umbra reduces the room's effective Umbra stage by the printed number of steps for the rest of combat.
It cannot reduce the effective stage below Clear.

entries.title: Tunnel Crawler
body: Fast close-range predator that closes distance and opens bleed wounds.
Its intents favor short movement paths followed by melee bleed attacks.

entries.title: Dust Acolyte
body: Ranged caster with dust bolt attacks, self-defense actions, and health-draining effects.
Its intents alternate between line-of-sight damage and preservation.

entries.title: Bone Harrier
body: Mobile ranged skirmisher with pierce and bleed attacks.
Its intents often combine repositioning with a ranged strike.

entries.title: Stone Warden
body: Durable front-line guard with heavy melee attacks, block gains, and close area strikes.
It can absorb damage through defenses before its health is exposed.

entries.title: Cinder Ooze
body: Fire ooze whose attacks leave persistent Fire. It can split into smaller droplets when killed.
Slag Shell consumes one revealed nearby Fire tile for extra Block. You can use or replace that Fire first.

entries.title: Cinder Droplet
body: Small Fire fragment spawned by a Cinder Ooze. Its attacks can leave Fire.
Droplets occupy normal board tiles and share the same terrain danger as other actors.

entries.title: Shale Bloomer
body: Earth controller that places Rubble and exposes targets. Its narrow terrain patterns obstruct routes without filling the room.
Shale Shell consumes one revealed nearby Rubble tile for additional Stoneskin. Remove that selected tile to deny the bonus.

entries.title: Chainbound Gaoler
body: Air-locked jailer that pulls, pushes, and restricts movement.
Its intents use forced movement and immobilize to alter reachable tiles.

entries.title: Grave Surgeon
body: Support enemy that heals or guards injured allies.
Its guard clears elemental terrain under the chosen ally, opening a safer position without removing Rubble.

entries.title: Frostglass Lancer
body: Long-range Ice striker that creates Ice and threatens later Freeze.
New Ice does not immediately Chill a stationary target. Move away before your next turn starts to deny setup. Its spear strike is physical; Refract Guard clears Ice beneath the Lancer.

entries.title: Zekarion, the Raging Tempest
body: Storm dragon whose Lightning attacks create and exploit Electrified terrain. Chain links enemies and relay tiles across gaps.
Its stronger Shock attack reveals a chosen Electrified fuel tile. Remove that tile to deny the added disruption; the base attack still resolves.

entries.title: Lightning Wisp
body: Lightning minion that seeds Electrified tiles as relays.
Capacitor Arc consumes selected nearby Electrified fuel to add Shock. Its exposed fuel can be replaced or used first.

entries.title: Worldspines
body: Tharokh raises attackable stone spires at fixed arena positions.
Faultline ruptures tiles around surviving Worldspines and then breaks the spires. Destroying a spire leaves local Rubble: a cleared blast threat can still constrain movement.

entries.title: Kindle Ground and Crownfire
body: Vyraketh’s Kindle Ground creates normal Fire tiles and marks their positions for the next Crownfire. Placement causes no immediate terrain damage.
Crownfire detonates marked Fire that remains. Replace or consume the Fire before it resolves, or leave the previewed blast area. Overlapping blasts hit each actor once.

entries.title: The Hollow Gale
body: Vaeloryx's Hollow Gale reaches across the entire arena.
It damages the player, then pushes them away from the dragon one tile at a time; hazards encountered along the route still trigger.

entries.title: Crystal Armor
body: Each damaging hit breaks one Crystal Armor layer instead of damaging health. Separate hits can clear it before a heavy strike.
Iskaldra can consume selected Ice beneath itself to build additional armor. Remove that visible fuel before its turn to deny the bonus.

entries.title: The Last Eclipse
body: Noctyrax temporarily forces the arena to Eclipse and immediately harms actors standing without Radiance.
Its Veilbound Acolytes vanish in the dark. Placed light, personal vision, truesight, and Umbra dispelling expose the battlefield and protect the player.

entries.title: Veilbound Acolyte
body: Shadow minion that fights beside Noctyrax and disappears when Umbra hides its tile.
Radiance and truesight reveal its position before its ranged needles and closing strikes resolve.

entries.title: Tharokh, the Worldspine
body: Earth dragon whose Worldspines reshape the arena.
Faultline threatens the ground around surviving spires. Breaking them early leaves Rubble but removes those blast centers.

entries.title: Vyraketh, the Cinder Crown
body: Fire dragon that covers selected tiles with Fire, then follows Kindle Ground with Crownfire.
Replace or consume marked Fire before Crownfire, or clear its blast area. Ordinary Fire remains a shared hazard until removed.

entries.title: Vaeloryx, the Hollow Gale
body: Air dragon boss that weaponizes forced movement.
Its opening gale sweeps the full arena and can drive the player through hazards.

entries.title: Iskaldra, the Rime Tyrant
body: Ice dragon protected by hit-counted Crystal Armor. Ice beneath the dragon can fuel additional armor.
Break armor with separate hits and deny its visible Ice fuel. Its Ice attacks require active Chilled to Freeze, following the same terrain timing as yours.

entries.title: Noctyrax, the Last Eclipse
body: Shadow dragon and final boss of the twenty-fourth depth.
Its Last Eclipse hides two Veilbound Acolytes and punishes unlit positions; preserved Radiance creates the intended counterplay.

entries.title: Board Surfaces
body: Tiles can hold Rubble and one elemental surface: Fire, Ice or Electrified. Light remains independent.
Surfaces persist until consumed, replaced, removed or combat ends. Painting the same surface again does not stack its strength. A new elemental surface replaces the old one.
Terrain is shared by every actor. Placing Fire or Ice beneath a stationary actor has no immediate hazard effect; entry or that actor’s eligible turn start activates it.

entries.title: Fire Tiles
body: Entering Fire deals 1 damage. Starting an turn on Fire deals 2 damage after Block clears. Large actors take one event per step or start, regardless of how many Fire tiles they occupy.
Fire persists until consumed or replaced. Placement alone causes no damage. Detonate converts selected Fire into a single direct blast.

entries.title: Ice Tiles
body: Entering Ice or beginning a non-Frozen turn on Ice applies Chilled while the actor remains supported by Ice.
Fresh Ice placed beneath a stationary actor does not activate Chilled. Leaving all supporting Ice or removing it clears Chilled.
An Ice hit against active Chilled applies Freeze after damage and consumes all Ice beneath the actor.

entries.title: Electrified Tiles
body: Electrified is a conductor, not an entry hazard. It is ready as soon as it is placed, including for a later action on the same card.
A damaging Lightning attack can travel through a cardinally connected Electrified region, striking its enemy occupants once and consuming that region.
Chain can additionally jump through individual relay tiles across gaps within its printed jump reach. Only used relay tiles are consumed.

entries.title: Rubble
body: Rubble increases walking entry cost to 2. Forced movement ignores this surcharge; Blink only checks its landing.
Rubble can coexist with any elemental surface. It persists until consumed or removed. A first step with fresh positive movement remains possible even when its full cost exceeds the allowance.

entries.title: Chilled
body: Chilled becomes active when an actor enters Ice or starts a non-Frozen turn on Ice. Painting Ice underneath an actor does not immediately activate it.
While actively Chilled, each direct hit deals +1 damage. Hits do not consume Chilled; leaving or removing all supporting Ice does.
An Ice hit against active Chilled applies Freeze after damage and consumes supporting Ice. Frozen actors use the doubled direct-damage rule instead.

entries.title: Detonate
body: Detonate consumes selected Fire and attacks the union of those tiles and their four cardinal neighbors. Each actor is hit once, even where blast areas overlap.
Detonate is direct Fire damage and can harm the player and illusions as well as enemies. Only selected Fire is consumed; nearby Fire does not automatically cause a room-wide reaction.

entries.title: Consume Surface
body: Consume Surface removes the selected matching terrain as an explicit cost. Its printed reward requires successful consumption.
Enemy fuel tiles are chosen when their intent is revealed. Removing that specific fuel denies its bonus; the enemy does not secretly select another tile.

entries.title: Relocate Surface
body: Relocation moves an existing surface from its source tile to a chosen legal destination, keeping its layer.
An elemental surface replaces the destination’s old elemental surface. Rubble remains independent. Moving Fire or Ice beneath a stationary actor does not trigger a hazard immediately.
